phases.title: Implement detection core: overlays, Louvain, cluster density

review_findings.message: Declared edges are keyed by base-node insertion indices but consumed as sorted-union positions: model::load interns nodes in table order (decisions, system_patterns, progress_entries, custom_data, code_nodes, then link endpoints), union_graph sorts the key universe (louvain.rs:113-125), yet base.edges are mapped by raw e.src/e.tgt (louvain.rs:132-134). Whenever insertion order differs from sort order -- any workspace containing custom_data or code_nodes rows, or link endpoints of a kind sorting before 'decision' -- every declared edge lands on the wrong node pair (trace: nodes [d1,d2,cd1] sort to [cd1,d1,d2], so edge (0,1) attaches cd1-d1 instead of d1-d2). Overlay pairs are translated through the NodeKey index (louvain.rs:157) and are unaffected. Existing tests pass only because their decision+progress_entry universes coincide. Fix: resolve e.src/e.tgt via base.nodes through the union index before keying pairs, and add a mixed-kind regression (decision+custom_data with a declared edge, asserting pair_strength lands on the right NodeKeys).
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: union_graph now translates both declared-edge endpoints through the NodeKey-to-union index (louvain.rs:137-146, the only raw-index consumption site); regression test declared_edges_attach_to_true_endpoints_when_orders_diverge (louvain.rs:636) builds an order-divergent universe and asserts true endpoint pairs carry the weights while raw-reuse pairs stay 0.0; test run and passed (15/15 louvain tests)

review_findings.message: Collapse self-loops are pushed twice: for a==b both super_adj[a].push((b,w)) and super_adj[b].push((a,w)) execute (louvain.rs:335-338), so a community's internal mass enters k, tot, comm_w[own], and m2 at 4*W_int instead of the 2*W_int the symmetric-replication convention yields. With a single push, super-level gains would be exactly 2x node-level gains (uniform doubling, sign-preserving), i.e. the textbook two-level objective; as written the objective is distorted -- internal cohesion is overweighted, making dense communities stickier and merge decisions biased relative to the spec's 'Louvain modularity optimization' (spec line 116). Still deterministic and monotone (it is a consistent delta-Q for a fixed, well-defined super-graph), so AC-2 holds. Fix: skip the second push when a==b.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: super_adj now pushes once for a==b behind an `if a != b` guard with an explanatory comment (louvain.rs:348-352), yielding the textbook two-level objective; 15/15 louvain tests pass including identical_clusters_on_repeated_db_runs

review_findings.message: co_retrieval groups grow the node universe with nodes absent from the base graph (union_graph extends keys from overlay groups, louvain.rs:113-118): retrieval_surfaces has no FK or uniqueness (schema.rs:205-211), so surfaces referencing deleted items persist as ghost nodes until phase 3 pruning, and a double-written event row double-counts a pair's ramp. The deliberate inclusion of overlay-only real items is correct and tested; the ghost-endpoint and double-write exposure should be an explicit decision (dedup per (ts,cmd,arg) group and/or skip unknown nodes) before phase 3 feeds real telemetry in.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: union_graph filters every overlay group member through base.contains(k) before extending the key universe (louvain.rs:113-123), so ghosts produce no node and no edges while real pairs still count the event; regression test surface_ghosts_do_not_extend_the_universe (louvain.rs:691) asserts decision-99 vanishes and pair strength equals 1.0 + co_weight(1); test run and passed

review_findings.message: scan_writes_only_schema_candidates hardcodes an 11-table sample, not all tables: active_contexts, active_context_history, code_nodes, product_context, product_context_history, session_closes, and all four FTS tables are unchecked. code_nodes is in scan's own read path (model::load feeds the graph), so a regression mutating it would pass. review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: snapshot() (scan.rs:438-493) enumerates every table from sqlite_master, renders full row content for all storage classes (blob as hex), and falls back to natural order for WITHOUT ROWID FTS5 shadows; the audit compares before/after for all tables except schema_candidates, guarded by a presence assert. cargo test schemas: 7 passed.

review_findings.message: The Jaccard identity's edge paths are implemented but untested: assign()'s greedy tie-break (Jaccard desc, then cluster member set asc, then stored sig asc), the one-row-one-cluster constraint (second cluster matching a taken row must insert a fresh row), and upsert's drift-removed path all lack tests. A future assign() refactor could break determinism or winner selection and every existing test would stay green. The implementation itself is correct and deterministic on read.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: assign_prefers_higher_jaccard_order_independently (higher-J row wins in both stored orders), assign_is_one_to_one_when_two_clusters_match_one_row (exact-J cluster wins, loser stages fresh, both orders), and upsert_records_removed_drift_against_previous_members (drift-removed asserted against the persisted row: sig refreshed, drift 1/1, stability 2->3) cover the requested cases. Retry-2 residual closed: assign_tiebreaks_equal_jaccard_distinct_clusters_by_member_set (scan.rs:608-626) constructs genuinely J-equal distinct sets (both 5/6 vs the row, verified by intersection/union math) and asserts the lexicographically smaller member set wins in both caller orders; comparator level 2 is clusters[a].cmp(&clusters[b]) (scan.rs:145), matching the test. cargo test schemas: 9 passed.

review_findings.message: No CLI-level test invokes 'engrams schema scan' — all 4 tests call scan(&conn) directly, so arg parsing, dispatch wiring (Command::Schema -> schemas::handle), and JSON serialization of the command output are unexercised; tests/cli.rs precedent covers every other command family at the binary level.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: test_schema_scan_stages_and_writes_nothing_else (tests/cli.rs:2176) drives the real binary (assert_cmd, stdout parsed as JSON), seeds a dense triangle via CLI + SQL fixture, asserts one candidate, stability 1->2->3 with gates_pass flipping only on the third sighting, stable cluster_sig across scans, and a write audit asserting zero row deltas outside schema_candidates. Quality notes: the CLI-level write audit is a 4-table delta count (schema_candidates/decisions/context_links/item_anchors), not the exhaustive snapshot - exhaustiveness remains in the unit-level scan_writes_only_schema_candidates; and the gates flip is asserted from gates_pass, not the failed_gates array (unit-level failed_gates pinning covers the shape). Fixture seeding anchors by SQL with a documented reason (anchor add would materialize code nodes and join a fourth member). Test run and passed.

review_findings.message: Staging upserts run outside a transaction: a mid-scan failure leaves earlier rows advanced and later rows not, and the next scan advances the advanced rows again, inflating their stability_count by one sighting. Repo precedent (import.rs) wraps multi-row writes in a transaction; one unchecked_transaction around the upsert loop fixes it.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: one unchecked_transaction wraps the whole upsert loop with commit after (scan.rs:231-279); any upsert error propagates via ? and drops the tx, rolling back all staged rows.

review_findings.message: parse_members accepts `code` members (kind_table maps 'code' to code_nodes, confirm.rs:50-60) and confirm inserts member_of edges with source_item_type='code' via direct SQL, but the phase-1 ontology (rel.rs:170-177) and the spec (specs/0002-schema-formation.md:188) define the member_of domain as decision/progress-entry/system-pattern/custom-data/schema - code excluded. The reported 'post-confirm scan = new sig stability 1' semantics (restart is reasonable: an evolved cluster must re-clear stability) is untested behavior.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: scan_after_confirm_excludes_confirmed_candidate_but_keeps_members (confirm.rs:685-714) runs scan() after confirm(): the consumed sig does not re-stage, and post-confirm coherence is pinned - the evolved cluster restages as decision:1,decision:2,decision:3,schema:1, restarting at stability 1 exactly as reported. phases.title: Add retrieval tiering and surfacing telemetry

review_findings.message: serde_json preserve_order is a GLOBAL behavior change, and one pre-existing output silently degrades: graph stats (src/ops/graph/mod.rs:92-96) serializes std HashMaps directly into json! (nodes.by_type, edges.by_relationship, edges.by_origin). Under the previous BTreeMap-backed Map those keys were emitted alphabetically regardless of HashMap iteration order; under IndexMap the emission order follows HashMap iteration, which is randomized per process (SipHash RandomState). Every run of `engrams graph stats` now has a different key order for those three objects. Verified: no in-repo test or gate byte-compares that output (tests use field access; no exact-string JSON assertions in tests/), so nothing breaks today, but cross-run byte determinism of CLI output is lost for that command, and this repo elsewhere treats run-twice-identical output as an explicit contract (scan-twice-identical tests, dogfood gates diff raw scan output). Any future HashMap-to-json! site silently inherits the same hazard. Fix: sort keys at the stats site (BTreeMap before json!) so the global feature's blast radius stays limited to the payload this phase actually ordered deliberately.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: graph stats now builds nodes_by_type/edges_by_relationship/edges_by_origin as BTreeMaps with a comment citing the byte-determinism standard (graph/mod.rs:84-96); reviewer ran `engrams graph stats` 3x on the live DB — stdout byte-identical across runs, keys alphabetical (by_type: code,custom_data,decision,pr,progress_entry,system_pattern). preserve_order remains intentional elsewhere (schemas-leads-prime, tier-led arrays).

review_findings.message: AC-7's And clause 'a query with no schema match returns exactly what it would have before this feature' is not met literally: two always-present keys were added to unchanged outputs. (1) The zero-hit query response now carries schema_matches: [] even when centroid_hits is empty (src/ops/query.rs:222-227; HEAD returned {results, miss_guidance} only). (2) miss_guidance now always includes schema_centroids: [] on no overlap (src/ops/query.rs:328-334). Schema-less queries therefore return different JSON shape than before. Fix: insert the keys conditionally when non-empty.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: keys now inserted only when non-empty (query.rs:222-231 zero-hit object, query.rs:334-341 miss_guidance). Reviewer behavioral proof on seeded temp DBs: no-schema DB zero-hit has neither key (miss_guidance keys: hint,top_tags,token_hits,recent_decisions,graph_hubs); seeded-schema DB with non-matching term also has neither key; centroid-overlap query returns the tier-led array with the schema hit first (type schema, overlap 1) and records retrieval_surfaces rows for schema + co-surfaced decisions plus schemas reinforce.

review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: strict_subset_of_confirmed_bails_already_confirmed (confirm.rs:883-907) stages {d1,d2,d3}, confirms it, then stages strict subset {d1,d2} (J=1/3) and asserts the 'already confirmed' bail plus exactly one schema row; gates pre-passed via the stage() helper so only the covenant runs. Test run and passed this re-review.

review_findings.message: The subset-bail is permanent with no escape hatch: confirmed_schemas (confirm.rs:75-105) reads all member_of edges with no status filter, and no command exists to move a schema out of 'active'. Retiring or archiving the parent - whether by SQL or a future command - would not free its territory because the guard ignores status. The tradeoff (block nested duplicates now; merge/split and adaptation deferred) is right for this release, but the guard should consider only active/needs_review schemas, or the permanence needs documenting.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: the bail's site now documents the permanence (confirm.rs:408-410): 'Claimed territory frees only via prune/archive - the v0.14 adaptation owns the retire path (decision 76); nothing in the confirm covenant un-claims it.' Tradeoff is on the record with an owner.

review_findings.message: A strict superset of a small confirmed schema escapes both guards and promotes a near-duplicate: the containment check is one-directional (candidate covered by schema) and J-dilution lets supersets of <=2-member knowledge schemas (or code-bearing ones) under 0.7. Reviewer behavioral repro: confirmed core-2 {d4,d5}, then confirm {d4,d5,d7} (J=2/3=0.667, covered=2/3) promoted a third schema over the same core (schemas core-2 and infra coexist). Recommend mirroring the containment check for the no-drift direction (confirmed schema's non-schema members all present in the candidate -> bail; must exclude schema-type keys from the confirmed side since a restaged candidate's knowledge members never include them), leaving drifted shapes to the 0.7 identity rule.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: guard rewritten three-way (confirm.rs:416-433): containment (covered==candidate len), mirrored full-coverage (covers==confirmed knowledge len, schema-key-excluded both sides per the review recommendation), and J>=0.7. Superset pinned by strict_superset_of_confirmed_bails_already_confirmed (confirm.rs:910-936, cites the reviewer repro; passing). Reviewer binary repro on a temp DB both orientations: superset {d1,d2,d3} over confirmed {d1,d2} bails naming schema 1; legitimate overlap {d1,d3,d4} over confirmed {d1,d2} (covered=1/3, covers=1/2, J=1/4) promotes as a second schema - the guard does not strangle independent concepts.

review_findings.message: Test-count claim off by one: '+7 unit tests' claimed, tree adds 6 (all in assimilate.rs; bin target 68->74, full suite 157->163, both reviewer-verified). Same genre as phase 7's count correction.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: suite count now matches the claim - reviewer ran the full suite this re-review: 166 passed / 0 failed across all 5 targets.

review_findings.message: The guard's safe direction is unpinned: no test asserts that a candidate merely OVERLAPPING a confirmed schema's territory (some shared members, no containment either way, J<0.7) still promotes - the exact scenario where the new mirrored coverage clause could over-fire and silently strangle independent concepts. Reviewer binary repro verifies the behavior today (overlap {d1,d3,d4} over confirmed {d1,d2} promotes); the regression needs its own pin.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified (Gate 4 re-review 2026-09-05): noted

phases.title: Round-trip schemas through export, import, and fresh DB

review_findings.message: member_of provenance does not survive the round-trip: confirm writes origin='manual' with source='schema_confirm', but no export SELECT carries the source column (links export and the per-schema members array both omit it) and neither import INSERT restores it - after import every confirm-created edge has source=NULL. Also the export.rs comment rationalizing the dedup design is factually wrong: it says the generic links export excludes confirm edges because they use origin 'schema_confirm'; in reality confirm edges carry origin='manual' and links/ carries them, which is exactly why the members-array NOT EXISTS guard is load-bearing. No code reads context_links.source today, so nothing misbehaves now; the column is the only durable distinction between human-made and confirm-made member_of edges, and the round-trip silently erases it.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: export now carries source on both paths (links files include confirm edges with origin manual + source schema_confirm; members array gained the source column) and import writes it back; reviewer round-trip repro shows 3/3 member_of edges on the target with source='schema_confirm', and the corrected comment states the real dedup mechanism. Residual note: no test asserts the source column on the target - s14 pins idempotency and dedup only; provenance verified behaviorally by this review.

review_findings.message: retrieval_surfaces import is not idempotent: the plain-INSERT loop duplicates every telemetry row on re-import (reviewer repro: 4 rows after first import, 8 after second), while every other entity in the importer is idempotent by construction (INSERT OR REPLACE with exported ids, members guard). Importing the same export twice - or overlapping exports - inflates the reward telemetry that gates and ranking consume. A WHERE NOT EXISTS on the natural key (ts, cmd, arg, node_kind, node_id) restores parity with the rest of the importer.
review_findings.resolution: resolved-verified: re-import guard on the natural key with null-safe arg IS ? binding. Reviewer repro (the original 4-to-8): after retry the same double-import yields surfaces unchanged (5 -> 5, including one NULL-arg row) and member_of unchanged at 3. s14 (tests/memory.rs:928-953) pins both counts across re-import and passes.

review_findings_resolved: member_of provenance now survives the round-trip: links export SELECT already carried `source`; members export SELECT gained it (`source_item_type, source_item_id, origin, source`), links import INSERT writes `source` back (import.rs:302-305), and the members NOT-EXISTS guard writes origin + source (import.rs:399-423). Wrong comment in export.rs replaced with the accurate one: links/ carries confirm edges (origin='manual', source='schema_confirm'); the members-array NOT EXISTS guard is the actual dedup and is load-bearing.

retrieval_surfaces import is now idempotent via the natural key (ts, cmd, arg, node_kind, node_id) with a null-safe `arg IS ?` guard, matching the importer's WHERE-NOT-EXISTS convention (import.rs:447-468). Pinned in S14: re-importing the same export leaves retrieval_surfaces count and member_of edge count unchanged (tests/memory.rs:928-953).
